title: Missile explosion kills two people in the Polish village of Przewodow near the Ukrainian border
body:
On Tuesday, 15 November 2022, at around 3:40 p.m., an explosion hit a grain facility in Przewodow, a village in south-eastern Poland about 6 kilometres from the Ukrainian border. Two Polish citizens were killed. The blast came as Russia fired dozens of missiles at cities across Ukraine, targeting energy infrastructure. It was the first explosion on the territory of a NATO member since Russia's invasion in February 2022.

Poland's foreign ministry said a Russia-made missile had caused the explosion. Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki said that a Russian provocation could not be ruled out. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg and US Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin said it was likely a Ukrainian air defence missile that landed in Poland, but both said that Russia bore ultimate responsibility because of its ongoing war against Ukraine.

The polskieradio.pl report gave no final investigation findings. Early press reports on the day differed. An Associated Press report cited a senior US intelligence official as saying Russian missiles had crossed into Poland, while the Pentagon said it could not confirm that. Stoltenberg and Austin made their assessments in the days that followed, after consultations among allies. Poland and NATO described the incident as the likely result of Ukraine defending itself against the Russian attack, and the exact origin of the missile remained the subject of investigation at the time of the report.
